clusters.summary: Gap: Users need troubleshooting and migration guidance when an older `.cursor/cli.json` prevents a Cursor thread from starting. Resolution: no confirmed auto-migration, stderr-display fix, or safe replacement configuration is supplied. Verify which keys are deprecated for the current cursor-agent version and whether T3 Code will surface the detailed error or migrate the file before documenting remediation steps.

## Working on T3 Code

Start with the [development runbook](./operations/development.md) and [contribution policy](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

Internal notes preserve architectural decisions, constraints, and implementation traps that the source alone does not explain. Most code changes do not need an internal documentation update. Follow the [documentation rules](../AGENTS.md#documentation) before adding one.

documentation_evidence.title: Updating T3 Code (docs/user/updating.md)
documentation_evidence.content:
# Updating T3 Code

The app you use and the server running your agents can be on different machines. When a server is behind your web or desktop app, an update notice appears in the conversation and **Settings → Connections**. Update the machine named in that notice.

## Before you update

Server updates restart the connection and can interrupt active agents and terminal commands. Saved threads, settings, and project files remain.

**Settings → General → Continue threads after restarts** is off by default. Enable it to resume supported active threads after an update, crash, or machine restart. Changes are saved to connected environments that support this setting; update older servers first. If a supported environment was offline or has a different value, use **Apply to all** in Settings after it connects. T3 Code must start again on that machine; the setting does not enable automatic startup. Terminal commands may still be interrupted, and threads without saved provider resume state need a new message. If you previously enabled continuation for updates, enable this setting once to allow recovery without a connected client.

## Update a connected server

The offered action depends on how the server runs:

clusters.name: export log records over OTLP
clusters.summary: Log records can now be exported over OTLP, configured the way traces and metrics already are: T3CODEOTLPLOGSURL, the desktop bootstrap envelope, or Settings, in that order of precedence. Logs share T3CODEOTLPHEADERS, T3CODEOTLPPROTOCOL, and the export interval with the other two
clusters.recurring_question: What changed, and what should users know about the shipped behavior?
clusters.draft_summary: Adds the missing configuration-source precedence and shipped behavior for OTLP logs, including desktop bootstrap and Settings configuration, logger replacement, and unchanged local persistence behavior.
clusters.draft_markdown:
### Configure OTLP log export

In addition to `T3CODE_OTLP_LOGS_URL`, the desktop client can provide the OTLP log endpoint through the desktop bootstrap envelope or Settings. When more than one source is present, the server uses this precedence order:

1. `T3CODE_OTLP_LOGS_URL`
2. The desktop bootstrap envelope
3. Settings

OTLP logs use the same `T3CODE_OTLP_HEADERS`, `T3CODE_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, and export interval as traces and metrics.

When a log endpoint is configured, the OTLP logger replaces `Logger.tracerLogger` rather than being added alongside it. As a result, a message emitted inside a recorded span is exported once as a log record instead of twice. In this mode, that message is no longer carried in the local trace file. With or without OTLP log export, stdout output and SSH-managed log persistence are unchanged.

## Sources

- [Merged PR #12493: feat(server): export log records over OTLP](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/12493)
- [Existing docs: Observability (docs/operations/observability.md)](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/cb3d95c17487f3d834a5537f7c3aa0106bc9b5ec/docs/operations/observability.md)

documentation_coverage.rationale: The observability page documents OTLP log export through `T3CODE_OTLP_LOGS_URL`, the shared headers and protocol settings, the export interval, the service name, and the fallback that leaves logs on stdout when URLs are unset. It does not explain the reported desktop bootstrap envelope or Settings configuration sources, their precedence, or the complete shipped configuration flow for logs alongside traces and metrics.

documentation_evidence.title: Settings and project overrides (docs/user/project-settings.md)
documentation_evidence.content:
r captures and rotated logs have separate retention periods. Expired capture links stop working. Current logs, message attachments, and browser profiles are kept.

## Project icons Select the project and open Project to choose an icon, emoji, monogram, or image. The choice applies to every checkout in the project group and appears on connected clients. Choose **Automatic** to let T3 Code detect an icon again.

Choose **Monogram** in the icon picker to set one or two letters or numbers and a color.

When no image is found, web and desktop show a two-character monogram with a color from the icon palette, derived from the saved project name. For example, `Nebula` becomes `NA`, `Silver Orchard` becomes `SO`, and `M7 Forge` becomes `M7`.

## Keep the default branch current

In Source Control, enable **Automatically pull** to keep the default-branch checkout up to date with its configured upstream. Choose an environment to set the default or a project to override it. On mobile, use **Settings → Source control** to change selected environment defaults or project overrides.

T3 Code only pulls when it can fast-forward and the checkout has no changed files, untracked files, or local commits. It skips checkouts on another branch or without an upstream. If a checkout has local work, resolve it yourself before automatic pulls can resume.

For a manual worktree or launcher without that link, export the same fixed value instead:

```sh export T3CODE_DEV_AUTH_TOKEN="<the value generated above>" ``` Do not generate a new value at startup. Start or restart `vp run dev --share` after configuration, then open its printed startup pairing URL once per browser profile on that hostname. Later web dev servers on the same hostname accept the shared cookie across ports. The cookie expires after 30 days. Reload an old tab if its URL now serves a replacement environment.

The token and startup pairing URLs are reusable administrative secrets. Never put them in a commit, pull request, or public output. Every server still seeds its own auth database record at startup and keeps its own SQLite data, signing key, and revocation state. Desktop and non-dev servers ignore the value. ```sh vp test run <files> vp lint <files> vp run --filter <package> typecheck ```

clusters.name: Provider-specific change request template support
clusters.summary: Gap: Documentation for Follow change request templates does not establish which hosting providers and repository template paths are supported. The issue reports that `GitManager.ts:2023` gates `detectPrTemplate` on `provider.kind === "github"`, and `PrTemplateDetection.ts` only checks GitHub-compatible paths. The affected paths are `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md` and `.azuredevops/pull_request_template.md`. Resolution: no confirmed implementation or documentation decision is supplied. Verify whether GitLab and Azure DevOps support is intended; then document the actual provider scope, setting behavior, and supported paths rather than implying that enabling the setting covers all providers.
clusters.recurring_question: Which hosting providers and repository template paths are honored when Follow change request templates is enabled?
clusters.draft_title: Follow change request templates: current provider scope
clusters.draft_summary: Documents the currently reported GitHub-only behavior and the repository paths checked for GitHub templates, while clearly flagging GitLab and Azure DevOps support as requiring maintainer verification.
clusters.draft_markdown:
### Follow change request templates: current provider scope

The **Follow change request templates** setting currently applies only when the project provider is GitHub. For GitHub repositories, template discovery checks these repository paths and directories:

- `.github/pull_request_template.md`
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
- `pull_request_template.md`
- `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
- `docs/pull_request_template.md`
- `docs/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`
- `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`
- `docs/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`

GitLab and Azure DevOps templates are not currently passed to the description generator, even when the setting is enabled. The reported unsupported paths are `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md` and `.azuredevops/pull_request_template.md`. The current workaround is to apply those templates manually when editing the generated request description.

**Maintainer verification needed:** confirm whether GitLab and Azure DevOps template support is intended, and if so, confirm the supported paths and final setting behavior before documenting cross-provider support.

## Resolution

From [issue #12330](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/12330):

Manually apply the template when editing the generated request description.

## Sources

- [Issue #12330: [Bug]: Follow change request templates ignores GitLab and Azure DevOps templates](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/12330)
- [Existing docs: Source control (docs/user/source-control.md)](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/cb3d95c17487f3d834a5537f7c3aa0106bc9b5ec/docs/user/source-control.md)

documentation_coverage.rationale: The source-control documentation covers provider-related review features, including GitHub stacks and Azure DevOps review requirements, but it does not document the Follow change request templates setting. Specifically unanswered are whether the setting is honored only for GitHub or also for GitLab and Azure DevOps, which repository paths and template directories are checked, and what happens when no supported template is found. The supplied implementation evidence indicates a GitHub-only gate and GitHub-style paths, but that behavior is not documented.

## An absence changes meaning at the provider boundary Below the boundary, in a patch parser or a response decoder, a missing path means this revision does not carry that file. Above it, in [`ProviderFileRevisions`](../../apps/server/src/pullRequest/PullRequestProvider.ts), a missing path means the read could not say. A provider's `getFileRevisions` converts on the way up: a path its host looked at and has no version for arrives as the empty string, and absence is kept for what the provider never got to look at. Absence below the boundary does not survive it.

What "never got to look at" is belongs to the host, and the contract cannot know any of them:

- [Azure DevOps](../../apps/server/src/pullRequest/AzureDevOpsPullRequestProvider.ts) reads every version off one iteration listing, so a change too long to follow to its end leaves the paths past that point out. - [Bitbucket](../../apps/server/src/pullRequest/BitbucketPullRequestApi.ts) reads them off the pull request's own patch, the only place it states a file's version, so a patch cut short at the byte ceiling leaves the paths past the cut out. - [GitLab](../../apps/server/src/pullRequest/GitLabPullRequestCli.ts) asks in batches, so a batch it could not read leaves that batch's paths out.

## GitHub stacks

The Pull Requests page shows each PR's position in its GitHub stack. Open the stack badge in a review to navigate its layers. **Merge stack** submits the selected pull request and every unmerged layer below it to GitHub together, respecting branch rules and merge queues. The confirmation shows the scope and merge strategy. GitHub rebases the remaining stack after merging.

clusters.name: Context-window indicator discoverability
clusters.summary: Gap: Users cannot see context-window usage in either main or branch/worktree threads, and there is no in-app notice or documented recovery path. The reported root cause is that PR #9190 introduced `contextWindowMeterEnabled` with a default of `false`, while `ChatComposer` passes `null` instead of the available context value. Resolution: no confirmed fix is supplied. Verify the intended default, the restore mechanism, and parity across thread types before documenting the behavior. The supplied issue does confirm the relevant location as Settings → General → Legacy features, but not the exact control or steps for restoring the indicator.
clusters.recurring_question: Why is the context-window indicator missing, and how can I monitor or restore it in main and branch/worktree threads?

documentation_coverage.rationale: The composer documentation explains that web and desktop can compact from the context meter and documents `/compact`, but it does not explain why the context-window indicator is absent by default, where to restore it, or whether it is available in both main and branch/worktree threads. The supplied implementation evidence identifies the control as Settings → General → Legacy features → Context window indicator (legacy), with a default of off, but that recovery path and thread-type behavior are not present in the retrieved documentation.

## Context in your message

Context you attach lands where your cursor is, as a chip inside your text: a terminal excerpt, a review comment from a diff or file, a preview annotation, or a file. You can type before and after a chip, move it by cutting and pasting, and delete it like a character. Hover a chip for its brief details. Select a terminal excerpt to open its captured output, or select a review comment, picked element, or preview annotation to open its full details. Chips read as "Terminal excerpt, Terminal 1 lines 3-4" and similar to screen readers.

nd the **Use reset** action in the account details. On narrow screens, numbered rows below the bar show each account's quota, countdown, and credits. Tap a row to open its details. The same account signed in on more than one environment, or reported by a hub as well, counts once. Filter with the environment dropdown to see what a single machine has.

Opening Limits checks the selected connected environments automatically. Each client waits at least five minutes between automatic checks of an environment, including after a failed check. If a window still looks stale, refresh Limits to re-check every provider and hub.

Pick `/usage-limits` from the composer's command menu, or send it as a message, to check the current model's limits without leaving the conversation. The result opens above the composer and closes when you dismiss it or send your next message. It uses the same snapshot as **Usage → Limits**, so it does not run the agent or refresh anything. The command is offered only for providers that appear under **Usage → Limits**.

docs_sources.title: Updating T3 Code (docs/user/updating.md)
docs_sources.snippet: # Updating T3 Code The app you use and the server running your agents can be on different machines. When a server is behind your web or desktop app, an update notice appears in the conversation and **Settings → Connections**. Update the machine named in that notice. ## Before you update Server updates restart the connection and can interrupt active agents and terminal commands. Saved threads, settings, and project files remain. **Settings → General → Continue threads after restarts** is off by default. Enable it to resume supported active threads after an update, crash, or machine restart. Changes are saved to connected environments that support this setting; update older servers first. If a supported environment was offline or has a different value, use **Apply to all** in Settings after it connects. T3 Code must start again on that machine; the setting does not enable automatic startup
